threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’re still taking photos of the street art, instead of walking past it like it’s the daily wallpaper.
Caught a late 333 last week; a guy was serenading the whole bus with a ukulele. Didn't know if I should join in or get off at the next stop!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the smell of fresh döner and currywurst mixed with the sound of street musicians on Sonnenallee at midnight. That’s when I knew.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous dance party at a bus stop during a BVG strike. It somehow turns the chaos into a community fest.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they greet the taco truck guy like an old friend, while the newcomers just stare at the menu.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a Muni driver hand a sandwich to a homeless guy at 16th Street. That’s the kind of empathy you don’t see enough in this city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love vermut. I've seen many turn their noses up at the stuff, preferring a simple canya instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their reluctance to embrace the siesta; you’ll see them hustling around at 3 PM, while locals linger over coffee.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep ordering a flat white but still ask for sugar, while everyone else has already switched to oat milk and sea salt.
Saw a couple on the 68 bus passionately arguing over a half-eaten kebab. Can't blame them; those late-night snacks can stir up some real emotions.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a flock of pigeons chilling at the bus stop, waiting for the next BVG strike to end. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice Kreuzberg cafés serve a free slice of cake with your coffee if it’s your birthday? You’d think it’s a gimmick, but people actually celebrate there!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local will know to carry a sweater in July; those fogs hit without warning, while newcomers just sweat in the sun.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 47 bus serenading the driver with a ukulele. They both smiled like it was a regular Tuesday. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the real charm in our local tavernes and hidden plazas where the rhythms of daily life pulse.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a ‘café amb llet’ but never realize it's just ‘café con leche’ here. The locals just smile knowingly.
